arya: quick heads-up — I'm running an experiment in us-west1-gpu to test a new 'graceful-shrink' downscaling policy. target: faster scale-to-zero for idle gpu pools (goal ~4m cooldown) while avoiding failed in-flight inference requests. seeing intermittent 504s from the gateway after nodes drain.

samir: can you paste the autoscaler config you applied? is this CA or a custom controller? :thinking:

arya: it's the cluster-autoscaler v1.26 with an overlay that we wrote for gpu affinity. snippet:```yaml
nodePool: gpu-pool-usw1
scaleDown:
  enabled: true
  gracePeriodSec: 240
  minUsagePercent: 20
  delayAfterAdd: 10s
  drainTimeout: 2m
```

lena: 2m drainTimeout + immediate eviction is suspicious for GPUs. CUDA driver unload / MIG teardown can take longer on some kernels. when eviction happens pods get rescheduled to small cpu-only fallback and the proxy times out. do you have node-local logs for kubelet + nvidia-uninstall?

arya: attaching quick traces: `kubelet: evicting pod X` -> `nvidia: driver teardown start` (18s) -> `nvidia: cuda-runtime wait` (2m 30s) -> `node gone` -> downstream gateway 504. so driver teardown is the culprit on certain GPU types.

miguel: suggestion: add a pre-drain hook to cordon but delay actual kernel teardown until pods are moved, or extend drainTimeout for nodes with active cuda pods. also consider marking pods with `node.kubernetes.io/no-evict` during short batch runs.

samir: we could also use a two-tier shrink: first, mark nodes as 'standby' (no new pods), wait X seconds for KV cache warm handoff, then drain. i.e. a prewarm->standby->drain flow. keeps prefix cache alive for short tails. averages out slower teardown.

arya: i like that. currently our warm-pool logic is binary. Implementation idea: add a state machine on the node object with states: ACTIVE -> STANDBY (60s) -> DRAINING (240s) -> TERMINATED. Policies per-pool.

lena: Another angle: avoid moving latency-sensitive pods at all. tag critical inference pods with `redwood/placement: sticky` and exclude them from scale-to-zero decisions. let them live on dedicated reserved nodes. saves cost if sticky set of pods is small.

miguel: tradeoff is reserved capacity cost. but we could auto-compact sticky pods into a small reserve pool and scale that slower. cheaper than repeated cold starts.

arya: has anyone measured the cost delta vs 504 recovery? quick napkin: each 504 customer retry costs ~0.05s of extra token compute + customer SLA noise. but a reserved 1-GPU node in us-west1 costs ~ $0.9/hour. if we keep 1 reserved for 20 customers we win. need real numbers.

samir: for rollout: 1) implement STANDBY state 2) set stanbyDuration=60s for first pass 3) special-case pods with `redwood/no-evict` 4) add telemetry to count driver-teardown time + gateway 5xx correlation 6) enable in canary region only (us-west1)

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: `infra/graceful-shrink-v1` -> canary=us-west1 -> ETA 15m.

arya: thanks — i'll push a PR with state machine and metrics. will also add a script to detect node images with long driver teardown and tag pools accordingly.

lena: +1. also please add a k8s job to run `nvidia-smi` + driver unload bench per image flavor so we can precompute teardown hazard.

samir: we should also update runbooks: emergency manual rollback is `kubectl annotate node <node> redwood/skip-terminate=true` to stop autoscaler from taking it and then `kubectl uncordon` once safe.

arya: noted. planning to merge tomorrow and run a 6h canary. will post results here. :rocket:
